newsitem.title: UK: Greece eyes jumbo yen bond - London bankers.
newsitem.headline: Greece eyes jumbo yen bond - London bankers.

text.p: Greece is taking bids for a large-sized yen bond issue, bankers said on Wednesday.
"Greece is looking to raise up to 120 billion yen ($1.1 billion)," a syndicate manager at a Japanese bank in London said.
Another said Greece was eyeing a 100 billion yen issue. Greece could opt for either a domestic Samurai bond or an international Euroyen issue, bankers said.
"Greece is interested in tapping as long a maturity as possible, maybe even beyond 20 years if it opts for a Samurai," a Euroyen dealer said.
Other possibilities included a shorter-dated Euroyen bond or a floating-rate note issue. A deal was likely to surface towards the end of July, bankers said.
In July last year Greece launched a total of 130 billion yen worth of Samurai bonds in three tranches via Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
The bonds had six-, 12- and 20-year maturities.
Greece is rated Baa1 by Moody's and BBB- by Standard & Poor's. ($ = 112.7 Japanese Yen)
